definitions.explanation: The act or posture of raising oneself up on the tips of the toes, either to reach something high or to walk quietly.

examples.japanese: つま{先立|さきだ}ち⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{棚|たな}→棚：01650_tana⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{手|て}を{伸|の}ばす→手を伸ばす：20169_tewonobasu⟧。
examples.english: To reach for the shelf on tiptoe.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}ども⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧つま{先立|さきだ}ち⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{窓|まど}→窓：02254_mado⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{外|そと}→外：00671_soto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{覗|のぞ}いていた→覗く：02388_nozoku⟧。
examples.english: The child was standing on tiptoe, peeking out the window.

examples.japanese: ⟦{赤|あか}ちゃん→赤ちゃん：01282_akachan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{起|お}こさない→起こす：01234_okosu⟧よう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、つま{先立|さきだ}ち⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{部屋|へや}→部屋：00507_heya⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{横切|よこぎ}った→横切る：02326_yokogiru⟧。
examples.english: I tiptoed across the room so as not to wake the baby.

notes:
Literally "tip-of-toe standing," from つま{先|さき} (tiptoe, toe tip) and ⟦{立|た}ち→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧ (standing). Used both for the physical action of raising oneself on tiptoe to reach something and for the quiet, careful walking associated with tiptoeing.

Often written in hiragana or mixed script (つま{先立|さきだ}ち) rather than full kanji ({爪先立|つまさきだ}ち). The verb form つま{先立|さきだ}ち⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ is also common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- つま{先立|さきだ}ち⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧: to walk on tiptoe
- つま{先立|さきだ}ち⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to stand on tiptoe
- つま{先立|さきだ}ち⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{覗|のぞ}く→覗く：02388_nozoku⟧: to peek on tiptoe

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{背伸|せの}び→背伸び：13930_senobi⟧: stretching up on tiptoe — often implies straining beyond one's natural ability
- ⟦{忍|しの}び{足|あし}→忍び足：16016_shinobiashi⟧: stealthy footsteps — walking quietly, with a nuance of secrecy
